zoe: quick flag from the reranker-lite bringup: int8 PTQ run on holdout shows NDCG@10 +0.7% but MRR@5 -2.8%. short-query slice dominates the MRR drop.
pranav: did you change any preproc or candidate curation?
zoe: not intentionally. i used the CI-provided preproc artifact. digging now.
alex: can you paste the eval command and the slice sizes?
zoe: ```
./eval_rerank --gold holdout_core.json --pred preds_reranklite_int8.json --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@5 --slices short_query:300,long_query:1200 --preproc-checksum ab12cd34
```
zoe: short-query slice is 312 qids.
pranav: what's the tokenizer and priming used (sentencepiece vs byte-bpe)?
zoe: sentencepiece_v1, priming: top-3 snippets, sanitizer: html_strip=true (from CI artifact).
pranav: interesting — earlier bringups that flipped sanitizer to keep tags showed similar short-query volatility. quantized models compress score margins; small tokenization/priming differences can flip top-k for short queries and hurt MRR.
alex: can you rerun a quick fp32 vs int8 parity with the exact same preproc artifact locally? also try forcing html_strip=false to see sensitivity.
zoe: reran both:
- fp32 (artifact ab12cd34, html_strip=true): ndcg +0.5 mrr -0.3
- int8 (artifact ab12cd34, html_strip=true): ndcg +0.7 mrr -2.8
- int8 (artifact ab12cd34, html_strip=false): ndcg +0.9 mrr -0.4
so toggling html_strip explains most of the MRR gap.
pranav: OK that nails it. mitigation: 1) onboarding checklist must assert preproc checksum parity between offline eval and staging canary, 2) add short-query int8 smoke (~250 qids) in CI that compares MRR against fp32 baseline with a loose threshold (e.g., fail if MRR drops >2%), 3) annotate model card: "sensitive to sanitizer/priming changes under quantization".
zoe: i'll open PRs for the checklist + CI smoke and update model card. i'll also upload diffs and failing ids to s3: s3://redwood-eval/artifacts/rerank-lite/1725555555/
ci-bot: staging snapshot created: snapshot-reranklite-2026-03-15-09-40 :rocket:
alex: thanks for the quick repro. we should also consider a tiny deterministic tie-breaker for quantized scoring if we keep seeing non-deterministic flips.
pranav: +1 on tie-breaker and checksum assert. good follow-ups.
